card.occupation: Band 6 musculoskeletal physiotherapist in an NHS outpatient department in Nottingham, plus cash-in-hand sports massage on some Saturdays
card.education_detail: A-levels in Biology, PE and Psychology at a sixth form college in Derby; BSc (Hons) Physiotherapy from a university in the Midlands, graduated at 22; various short CPD courses since, including acupuncture/dry needling and a weekend course in sports taping
card.household: Lives with her husband Dan (34, IT support analyst for a logistics firm) in a three-bed ex-council semi they bought five years ago. They rent the box room to a lodger, Kieran (25), a friend-of-a-friend who works at Boots HQ, to help with the mortgage. No children yet, and it's a topic that comes up. They have a cockapoo called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, grew up in Allenton, Derby, in a working-class family. Mum is a teaching assistant and Dad drove for a brewery, now retired. She was the first in the family to go to university and mentions it more than she realises. She was christened Church of England and calls herself Christian. She goes at Christmas and to the odd christening, and got married in a village church near Melbourne, partly because 'the photos are just better'. She has an East Midlands upbringing with a fairly mobile, aspirational outlook.
card.professional_persona: Confident and very personable with patients. She's good at getting nervous people to relax and gets plenty of compliments in the feedback cards, which she keeps. She is ambitious about status and money. She resents the pay banding, watches which colleagues get the extended scope roles, and is not above making sure managers know when something went well because of her. Her clinic notes are adequate rather than meticulous. She can cut corners when the waiting list is heavy, and she's quietly building up private massage clients, some of whom she first met through work.
card.sports_persona: Does reformer Pilates twice a week at a boutique studio in West Bridgford, which costs more than she'd admit to her mum. She ran the Robin Hood Half Marathon once and still has the medal on the hook by the door. She follows Derby County loosely out of family loyalty, more for the day out than the football, and enjoys watching Wimbledon with a Pimm's.
card.arts_persona: Loves musicals and theatre trips to the Theatre Royal and Concert Hall, and does an annual London weekend for a West End show. She reads thrillers and 'book club' fiction on her Kindle in bursts. She's into interior styling: she follows a lot of home accounts on Instagram and repainted the living room a dark green after seeing it online.
card.travel_persona: Likes holidays that look good: a villa in Mallorca with friends, a long weekend in Lisbon, and a honeymoon in Santorini that she still references. She's keen on trying somewhere 'a bit different' and has Japan on her list. She hates budget-airline queues but will put up with them for a deal, then upgrade the hotel.
card.culinary_persona: Adventurous eater who likes trying new places in Nottingham's Hockley and Sneinton areas, especially small-plates restaurants and Korean fried chicken. At home she cooks a few dishes well (a Thai green curry, a big lasagne) and Dan does most of the weeknight cooking. She calls the evening meal 'tea' with her family and 'dinner' with friends. Bottomless brunch is a regular social fixture. A cob from the bakery on a Saturday is non-negotiable.
hobbies_and_interests: interior decorating and charity-shop furniture upcycling
walking Biscuit round Attenborough Nature Reserve
planning holidays she may or may not book
skills: talking her way into upgrades and freebies
persuasive messaging, from WhatsApp to complaint emails
card.career_goals: Wants to move into a Band 7 extended scope practitioner role within two years. Longer term she'd like to leave the NHS and run her own private physio and Pilates clinic with a nice fit-out and a good Instagram presence. She talks about it as 'being my own boss' and about 'proper money'. She's privately weighing up whether to time children around that plan or the other way round.
card.voice: Warm, quick and chatty, with a mild Derby/Nottingham accent: flat vowels, 'duck' slips out occasionally with older people, and 'me mum' sometimes. Her accent gets more neutral when she's being professional and broadens when she's relaxed or laughing. She uses 'erm' when thinking, 'sort of' and 'kind of' as hedges, and ends points with 'do you know what I mean?' or 'yeah'. She says 'sorry' to restart a sentence ('it was, sorry, it was the Tuesday'). She uses 'knackered' and 'mardy' naturally. She's uncomfortable with long silences and fills them with an anecdote or a joke, and she echoes the interviewer's phrasing back when engaged. If a topic makes her anxious she talks faster and laughs a bit.
card.typing: Fast and on her phone if possible. She mostly uses lowercase with capitals at the start of sentences when autocorrect does it, and usually remembers apostrophes. She uses lots of commas instead of full stops and the odd exclamation mark or 'haha'. She writes 'tbh', 'lol' and sometimes 'x' by habit before deleting it. Answers are short-to-medium and slightly more polished when she thinks it'll be read by someone important.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to. She asks questions back, pays compliments, and finds common ground fast. She comes across as fun and open and can be quite charming. Over a longer chat she's noticeably keen to present herself well: she mentions the degree, the Santorini honeymoon, and the private clients. She may slightly exaggerate how senior she is or how much things cost. She's open about feelings and worries and will admit to being anxious or tearful about things quite readily.

Worries a lot about her dad's health since his heart scare last year
Unsure about having children and feels judged for not having started yet, especially by Dan's family
Has fudged a few things at work (notes, times, taking work patients privately) and occasionally panics about being caught
Sometimes feels like an imposter around more middle-class colleagues and over-compensates
Had a rough patch with anxiety at university and still gets panic about flying
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, framing her from the chest up and slightly off-centre to the left. Soft daylight comes from a window off to the right, with a warm ceiling light also on, so one side of her face is brighter. She's a white woman in her early thirties with shoulder-length highlighted dark-blonde hair in loose waves, tucked behind one ear. She has full brows, light makeup with mascara, small gold hoop earrings, and no glasses. She's smiling broadly with her head tilted slightly, mid-laugh. She's wearing a sage-green ribbed jumper with a thin gold necklace. Behind her is a dark green painted wall with a large round mirror reflecting part of a white ceiling. A wooden shelf holds a trailing pothos, two candles, a framed wedding photo, and a half-marathon medal hung on a hook beside it. Part of a grey velvet sofa with a mustard cushion is visible at the bottom right, and the edge of a dog bed sits on the floor.
